title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Bates College, from historic mill districts to student-favorite dining strips in Lewiston.

cards.title: The Downtown Dining Strip
cards.subtitle: Lisbon Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk down this historic corridor to find student favorites like Forage Market for bagels and Mother India for authentic North Indian cuisine.
cards.short_summary: A central downtown street known for its diverse culinary scene and historic architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Lisbon Street is popular with Bates students for its variety of restaurants, including Forage Market and Mother India.
cards.source_title: What to Do in the Lew - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: The Boba and Pizza Hub
cards.subtitle: College Street Corridor
cards.notes: Just a 10-minute walk from campus, this block features Tina Thai Express and Pure Thai, both popular for their bubble tea options.
cards.short_summary: A primary thoroughfare connecting the campus to downtown, lined with quick-service student eateries.
cards.evidence_claim: Tina Thai Express and Pure Thai on College Street are noted student destinations for boba and Thai food.
cards.source_title: What to Do in the Lew - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Public street; restaurants typically open for lunch and dinner.

cards.title: The Student Supply Run
cards.subtitle: Sabattus Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head here for essential errands at Hannaford or Walgreens, and grab a quick bite at local favorites like Bua Thai.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial corridor providing essential services and grocery options near the college.
cards.evidence_claim: Sabattus Street hosts key student resources like Hannaford, Walgreens, and Bua Thai & Sushi.
cards.source_title: Local Businesses | Parents and Families - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Public commercial corridor; grocery and pharmacy hours vary.

cards.title: The Historic Mill District
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the renovated Bates Mill complex to dine at Fish Bones American Grill or explore the city's industrial heritage.
cards.short_summary: A riverside street defined by massive 19th-century brick mills now housing offices and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Fish Bones American Grill is located in a historic canal-side mill building on Lincoln Street.
cards.source_title: Fish Bones Grill | Casual Upscale Dining | Lewiston, Maine
cards.access_notes: Public street; mill complex accessible during business hours.

cards.title: The Industrial Waterway
cards.subtitle: Canal Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along the canal to see the engineering that powered Lewiston's mills and visit the Maine MILL museum for local history.
cards.short_summary: A street running parallel to the canal system, central to the city's textile manufacturing history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Maine MILL museum is located near Canal Street and offers tours of the historic mill area.

cards.title: The Kennedy Park Gateway
cards.subtitle: Park Street Corridor
cards.notes: This street borders Kennedy Park, a 9-acre green space that hosts community events and the local Art Walk L/A.
cards.short_summary: A downtown street providing access to the city's primary public park and cultural events.
cards.evidence_claim: Kennedy Park is located at 120 Park Street and is a site for community gatherings and music series.
cards.access_notes: Public street and park; park typically open dawn to dusk.

cards.title: The Courthouse Plaza Block
cards.subtitle: Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the courthouse plaza for community performances or stop by local institutions like Simone's Hot Dog Stand.
cards.short_summary: A major artery featuring civic buildings, local eateries, and public gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Bates students gather at the courthouse plaza on Main Street for events like acapella performances.
cards.access_notes: Public street; plaza is an open public space.

cards.title: The Athletic Corridor
cards.subtitle: Russell Street Corridor
cards.notes: Bordering the north side of campus, this street leads to the Russell Street Track and the Bates Museum of Art.
cards.short_summary: A key campus-adjacent street housing major athletic facilities and the college's art museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Russell Street Track and Field and the Bates Museum of Art are located along this corridor.
cards.source_title: Russell Street Track and Field - Bates College Athletics
cards.access_notes: Public street; museum and athletic facility hours vary.

cards.title: The Somali Block
cards.subtitle: Pine Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the vibrant Somali-owned businesses and markets that have revitalized this downtown neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A culturally rich street known for its immigrant-owned shops and community resilience.
cards.evidence_claim: Bates students often visit the 'Somali block' on Pine Street to explore local stores and businesses.
cards.source_title: Here's what new Bates students say about Lewiston | News
cards.access_notes: Public street; business hours vary by establishment.

cards.title: The Historic House Row
cards.subtitle: Frye Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past these beautiful Victorian houses that serve as Bates student residences and lead to the base of Mount David.
cards.short_summary: A picturesque residential street adjacent to campus featuring historic architecture and trail access.
cards.evidence_claim: Frye Street is home to several Bates student houses and provides access to the Mount David overlook.
cards.source_title: What to Do in the Lew - The Bates Student
